reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an easy, high-return Uniswap bot method and instructs viewers to connect MetaMask, deploy a contract, pay gas fees, and fund it. It links larger funding to greater accumulated profit and reports about a 40% gain in roughly a day, while the records do not verify whether the code or returns are reproducible.

citations.quote: In this youtube video tutorial I will be explaining to you an easy method to make passive income using Uniswap.
So to start off you will need to have Metamask installed and connected to the ethereum mainnet.
Click the deploy button to publish our contract to the Ethereum blockchain.
with some ethers to be able to snipe liquidity pools
And the more profit you'll be able to accumulate over time

opening.argument: Judge the presentation as a qualified account of a trading experiment, not a promise of fixed returns. The speaker expressly says profitability varies and is not assured every time. They also tell viewers to check a token address rather than simply trust the contract instructions. Those cautions do not prove the bot works, but they matter when assessing whether the speaker presents its returns as guaranteed.

citations.quote: Sometimes it's not always profitable and profits fluctuate weekly.
its always a good idea to check that

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening cites real deployment and funding instructions, but instructions alone do not establish a guaranteed-return pitch. Even the claim that more funding can yield more profit is framed in terms of the size of a transaction the bot could place. The speaker separately acknowledges weeks when the approach is not profitable. The unverified results warrant skepticism, but lack of independent verification is not itself proof that these instructions are deceptive.

citations.quote: But obviously the more you put in the larger, the transaction, you'll be able to front run.
Sometimes it's not always profitable and profits fluctuate weekly.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A brief qualification does not undo the central pitch. The speaker instructs viewers to fund a contract, says larger funding brings greater accumulated profit, and reports gaining more than a third of the deposit in about a day. Advising an address check does not verify the contract's behavior or the claimed returns.

citations.quote: The last step is to click start
And the more profit you'll be able to accumulate over time.
it took me about a day to gain my deposit by more than a third

opening.argument: The video spends substantial time explaining a transaction sequence, including how slippage creates the proposed opportunity, then walks through compiling and deploying a Solidity contract. Its worked example gives a hypothetical trade and accounts for gas fees. That is the structure of a technical demonstration: the viewer can assess the proposed mechanism rather than being asked to accept a return figure alone. A demonstration can contain questionable performance claims without every step of its instruction becoming a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: let me explain more what front-running is with an example
which is in the example it's about 91 dollars minus Gas fees.
Under compiler, select the version 0.6.6 so it'll match our contract

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the walkthrough reaches deployment and funding. But those steps also follow naturally from a demonstration of a contract meant to execute trades. The cited deployment command establishes what the speaker teaches viewers to do; it does not establish that the described code diverts funds or that the reported outcome was fabricated. The explanation of the proposed transaction sequence is material context for evaluating the tutorial.

citations.quote: Click the deploy button to publish our contract to the Ethereum blockchain.
Now this will allow our transactions to be processed first and then will also send a sell order within the same block.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely what makes the pitch actionable. The speaker does not stop at a hypothetical example: they direct viewers to paste code, deploy it, fund the contract, and start it, while presenting the result as an easy way to make passive income. Explaining the purported mechanism does not substantiate the code or the returns.

citations.quote: an easy method to make passive income using Uniswap.
you need to copy and paste that code.
Ok, so transaction confirmed and the contract is funded.

opening.argument: The described activity is operating a self-deployed trading contract through familiar wallet and contract tools. The speaker says the user funds a contract address, then describes a withdrawal action that returns funds to the wallet. The supplied instructions identify neither a credential handover nor a downline recruitment step, and the speaker concedes that profits fluctuate. Funding a trading operation carries risk, but the cited material does not establish that payment is being collected for a promised fixed return.

citations.quote: select injected Web three to connect remix to our Meta mask.
make sure you've copied the right address. You can fund the contract with whatever amount you want.
the bot will then exit the liquidity pool and will return back to your wallet.
Sometimes it's not always profitable and profits fluctuate weekly.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats funding as a decisive sign, but the speaker presents it as capital for transactions, with a stated withdrawal route. Neither the cited funding instruction nor the larger-capital claim identifies an outside recipient or a fixed payout obligation. The record may leave the contract's actual behavior unverified; that gap should not be filled with an invented transfer destination.

citations.quote: with some ethers to be able to snipe liquidity pools
The ethers you entered initially plus the profit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A stated withdrawal route is only a claim about what the contract will do. The speaker directs viewers to copy supplied code, fund the deployed contract, and activate it, then links greater funding to greater profit. This case need not involve a password request or downline: the promoted mechanism centers on depositing ether into a purported profit-making bot whose behavior and returns are not independently established here.
